title: Deathless transgenesis: a new spermatogonia mediated _in vivo_ approach for generation of transgenic mice
protocol: Transform DH5α competent cells with appropriate plasmid containing gene of interest.
Inoculate a colony of transformed bacteria in LB broth and add appropriate antibiotic.
Culture at 37°C with shaking at 220 rpm for 12-14 h.
Make bacterial stocks in 15% glycerol from autoclaved 80% glycerol stock.
Snap-freeze the bacterial stocks in liquid nitrogen.
Store bacterial stocks at -70°C for future use as inoculums.
Isolate plasmid from 3ml or 100ml cultures using QIAGEN Purification kits following manufacturer's instructions.
Check purity of plasmid on 1% TAE gels at 100-120V using submarine gel electrophoresis system.
Cut plasmid DNA with suitable restriction enzyme(s) for linearization.
Resolve the fragments of DNA on a 1% TAE agarose gel.
Run molecular weight marker in one of the lanes.
Excise a portion of gel containing DNA fragment of desired size using a clean sterile scalpel.
Elute DNA in about 30 μl of distilled water using QIAquick gel extraction kit following manufacturer's instructions.
Pull micro injection pipettes using the P-97 micropipette puller from Sutter Instrument Co.
Heat and pull borosilicate glass capillary in the heating chamber surrounded by a platinum heating element.
Polish the tip of the pulled pipettes to achieve a tip diameter of about 40-60 μm.
Anesthetize male mice intra-peritoneally with an appropriate dose of anesthesia (100 μl/20g body weight).
Remove hair from lower abdominal area.
Clean the area with Savlon and betadiene.
Give a cutaneous cut ventrally in the lower abdominal area under aseptic conditions using sterile surgical instruments.
Traverse abdominal muscles with a minor cut.
Pull the fat pad associated with the testis from the lower side of the abdominal cavity with curved forceps.
Place both exteriorized testes on a sterile autoclaved paper.
Use a 30 gauge needle to puncture the outer covering of the testicular tissue by a prick to facilitate insertion of a fire-polished glass micropipette.
Deliver a solution containing DNA and Trypan blue dye (0.04%) into the inter-tubular spaces of the testis through the glass micropipette.
Inject from 3 different sites to ensure maximum distribution of the DNA solution in the testis.
Inject about 10-15 μg of DNA into a testis.
Wait for 30 seconds after each injection before pulling out the pipette to prevent back flow of the DNA solution.
Hold the testis with a sterile tweezer-type electrode attached to an electroporator.
Deliver mild electric pulses to the testis.
Inject 20-35 μl of linearized DNA (0.5 μg/μl) into the testis of 30+2 days old FVB male mice.
Apply 8 square 40V electric pulses in alternating direction, changing pole after every 4 pulses.
Place the electroporated testis back in its original location.
Surgically remove the contra-lateral testis by hemicastration.
Tie the blood vessels with sterile nylon thread before hemicastration to prevent bleeding.
Give appropriate sutures to close both internal and external wounds.
Keep the tissue wet with sterile normal saline during the procedure.
Apply Neosporin at the site of sutures.
Keep mice under a candescent lamp for about 1 hour to provide warm temperature for revival from anesthesia.
After 30 days of electroporation, cohabitate electroporated animals with 2-month-old wild-type females for mating.
Take tail biopsies (2-3 mm) from 3-week-old pups.
Incubate tail biopsies at 55°C for 16 hours in high salt digestion buffer containing 50 mM Tris HCl, 1% SDS, 100 mM NaCl, 100 mM EDTA, and 1200 μg/ml Proteinase K.
Aliquot proteinase K in volumes of 200 μl and store at -20°C.
Process the lysate for DNA isolation by phenol-chloroform extraction followed by ethanol precipitation.
Quantify the DNA concentration of the extracted DNA by UV absorption at 260nm.
Check the purity of the DNA by A260/280nm ratio using a UV spectrophotometer.
Dilute the isolated gDNA to a final concentration of 200ng/μl and use as stock solution for running PCR using transgene-specific primers.

Prepare an optimal reaction mixture containing 1X Taq buffer, 0.2mM each dNTPs, 0.25μM of each reverse and forward transgene specific primer, 0.06U Taq DNA polymerase and 20ng of plasmid or 200ng of gDNA as template.
Mix the reaction mixture well and spin down briefly.
Carry out the PCR reaction in a Peltier Thermal Cycler PTC-200 with heated lid.
Set the PCR cycle conditions with respect to your primers.
Analyze the PCR products on 1.5% - 2% TAE agarose gel.
Include negative controls such as PCR with gDNA of wild type mice and a reaction without DNA in each set of PCR.
Use purified plasmid containing the respective transgene as a positive control.
Mate PCR positive pups from F1 generation with WT females to generate next generation of progeny.
Make homozygous line by inbreeding of transgenic littermates.
